main_body: Autumn tree: large orange-red leaf canopy (rows 0-28) on a thin brown trunk (rows 28-44) with a small base plinth
top_band: Canopy top: lighter orange clumps at rows ~1-10 rising to the crown, then darker red-orange mass below. The top reads as a rounded dome, but there is no distinct flat horizontal band
evidence: Organic tree: the canopy is a lit dome with lighter clumps on top and darker shaded underside, with a dark under-canopy shadow around rows 24-28 above the trunk. The trunk is a vertical column with a lit left and a dark right. A tree has no flat top surface to measure, and the canopy volume reads as 3/4 like the Beodeul tree references. No receding side face is drawn.

style.evidence: The canopy has about 5 orange/red steps with clumped dithering and a dark red-brown outline that matches the leaves, which is in the Beodeul manner. But it is a single smooth blob mass with little leaf-clump definition compared to the references, which have distinct leaf clusters, branches and root flare. The trunk is a plain straight column of 3-4 browns with a near-black outline, no branches, no roots and a flat plinth base, so it looks thinner and more sticker-like than the references. The trunk is the weakest area.
